commitResults.messageTitle: Add school levels to student records
commitResults.messageBody:
Allow tutors to supply an optional school level when adding or editing a student. Store and display the value so it is available in the student record and command feedback.

Use a default value for older JSON data that does not yet contain a school level. This preserves existing saved data while allowing future records to include the new academic information.

Add parser, model, storage, and command tests, and document the l/ prefix in the User Guide.
Add command to schedule a student's next lesson

Introduce a Subject value object and store it as part of each student record.

Persist subjects in JSON and use a default value when loading existing data files that do not contain the new field. This keeps previously saved TutorTrack data usable while preparing the model for command support in a later increment.

Add model and storage tests for subject validation, equality, persistence, and legacy-data compatibility.

Allow tutors to provide an optional subject through the s/ prefix when adding or editing a student.

Extend parsing and edit descriptors to validate subjects, reject repeated values, and preserve notes and next lessons when a subject is changed.

Add command-parser and descriptor coverage for valid, invalid, and repeated subject input.

Show each student's subject in the card and include it in command feedback so the academic field is visible after an add or edit.

Document the optional s/ prefix and add card-formatting coverage. This completes the subject information workflow from command input to persisted display.
Reject duplicate note prefixes and verify note persistence
Change shadowjar name

Model optional school-level and subject criteria together with required tags.

A student matches only when every supplied criterion is satisfied. This keeps
filtering rules independent of command parsing and provides focused coverage
for matching, non-matching, and empty criteria.

Introduce the filter command for matching students by school level, subject,
and required tags.

Reject commands without criteria and preserve the existing filtered-list
behaviour, so other index-based commands continue to operate on the displayed
results.

Describe filter criteria, AND-matching behaviour, and examples in the User Guide.

Add the command to the reference table so tutors can discover how to return
to the full student list after applying a filter.

Add a sequence diagram that traces parsing filter criteria, constructing the student-matching predicate, and applying it through the model. This keeps the Developer Guide aligned with the filter feature.
Combine the two invalid-input branches because both report the same usage message. This preserves the parser behaviour while making the validation easier to read and maintain.

Cover blank values, invalid tags, unexpected preambles, and partial tag matches so filter validation and matching behavior do not regress.

Document repeatable manual checks for combined criteria, empty results, errors, and resetting the filtered student list.
Configure the Gradle run task to enable Java assertions during local application runs. This allows internal assumptions to be checked while developing and testing TutorTrack.
Enable assertions for Gradle runs

commitResults.messageTitle: Preserve ongoing lessons when loading saved data
commitResults.messageBody:
Saved lessons were discarded as soon as their start passed,
allowing a conflicting booking after a restart. Keep them until
their end while retaining the past-start rule for new bookings.

commitResults.messageTitle: Inject a clock into lesson time checks
commitResults.messageBody:
Booking validation, loading and upcoming selection previously read
the system clock independently, making boundary tests unreliable.
Supply a shared local clock at startup and fixed clocks in tests.

The scheduling commands mixed index checks, clash detection and
updates in their execute methods. Extract focused validation
helpers while preserving clash order and rejected-command state.

The recurring command depended on the next-lesson command for a
shared error message. Move the wording to Messages so both commands
use the same stable text without depending on each other.

commitResults.messageBody:

Verify that an ongoing lesson remains stored immediately before its end and is discarded at its exact end, preserving the half-open timetable interval rule.

commitResults.messageTitle: Detect clashes between students' next lessons
commitResults.messageBody:
Next lessons can overlap without warning, allowing the tutor to book
conflicting sessions across different student records.

Reject overlapping next lessons before changing the model. Compare each
lesson's actual duration across all students, including filtered-out
records, while allowing adjacent lessons and replacing a student's own
lesson. Handle intervals that cross midnight and identify the conflicting
student in the error message.

Add logging, regression tests, and User Guide examples. Correct existing
Checkstyle violations so the style checks pass.

Focused tests and the documentation build pass. The full suite passes
399 of 400 tests; the existing JavaFX image-loading test fails locally.

Recurring schedules can overlap next lessons and other weekly schedules
without warning, allowing conflicting bookings in the tutor's timetable.

Check both scheduling commands against all student records before saving.
Use actual lesson durations and handle midnight and week boundaries while
allowing adjacent lessons. Treat a student's next lesson at the exact
weekday and start time of their own recurring rule as the same occurrence.
Exclude the old schedule when replacing a recurring lesson.

Identify the conflicting student and schedule in rejection messages. Add
logging, regression tests, and User Guide documentation for these rules.

Scheduling tests, Checkstyle, and the documentation build pass. The full
suite passes 412 of 413 tests; the existing JavaFX image test fails locally.

The Developer Guide lacks a diagram showing how both scheduling commands
validate input and reject conflicts before updating student records.

Add an activity diagram covering parse and index errors, next-lesson and
recurring-schedule comparisons, conflict rejection, and model updates.
Explain replacement exclusions and the same-student occurrence exception.
Reuse the shared PlantUML style and reference the diagram from the guide.

Build all documentation pages and inspect the generated diagram to verify
that it renders correctly and reflects the implemented command flow.
